name: Florida
$scopeNote: Florida has NO state individual wage income tax -- a constitutional prohibition (Fla. Const. Art. VII, sec. 5), not a mere policy choice. Never has had one.
exemptPretaxComment: Not applicable -- no income tax exists for any pretax category to reduce the base of.

reciprocity.note: Not applicable -- Florida has no income tax to be reciprocal about, same convention as this project's other no-income-tax states (SD, TN).

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE, and constitutionally barred. No Florida city or county levies, or may levy, a tax on wages or earned income.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE mandatory, and none permitted locally either. The Florida Paid Family Leave Insurance Act authorizes licensed insurers to OFFER voluntary paid-leave policies -- no state fund, no mandatory deduction (same voluntary-insurance-only shape as South Carolina's Act 206 and Tennessee's 2023 Act). Florida additionally preempts local governments from creating their own paid-leave mandates -- CONFIRMED directly via Fla. Stat. sec. 218.077's own text (see sources above), not just cross-sourced: 'a political subdivision may not... require an employer to... provide employment benefits not otherwise required by state or federal law.'

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset, built 2026-09-28 for prior-year corrections and retro pay. Only the fields the engine computes from were re-sourced for 2025 (suiEmployer). Descriptive fields (localIncomeTax.rule, reciprocity, paid-leave notes) are carried from the 2026 file; none of them changed between the two years.
